## Business dinner — Ostra
- **Why it fits:** Ostra is the polished, client-appropriate choice: its official site calls it an “elevated, coastal seafood dining experience,” says the dining room has “style and sophistication,” and notes a private room for up to 48 seated guests. Google Maps describes it as a “Sophisticated venue” for Mediterranean fish-focused fare and shows a 4.7 rating.
- **Price level / ceiling:** Google Maps reports **$100+ per person**. The current menu supports a high-end but controllable spend: mains run from **$36** (Cornish game hen) to **$150** for salt-crusted branzino for two; caviar is an optional splurge at **$115–$230**. A normal client dinner can readily be planned below your **$500-per-person** ceiling, though that ceiling could be exceeded if you add top caviar and premium wine.
- **Michelin Guide check:** I opened Michelin’s current Boston/Massachusetts restaurant index. It currently returned “no selected restaurants” for the searched Boston area, so I could not honestly represent Ostra as Michelin-starred or Michelin-selected. I chose it as the clearly polished fine-dining-tier alternative the prompt allowed, based on the restaurant’s own description, current menu, and Maps listing.
- **Availability in the next two days:** **Not confirmed online.** Ostra’s site has a “Reserve Now” call-to-action, and Google Maps shows “Reserve a table,” but the live booking times did not render in the browser. Call **(617) 421-1200** or use the open official/Maps pages to check September 30 or October 1.

## Anniversary dinner — Mamma Maria
- **Why it fits:** This is the more intimate, personal anniversary choice: its official site explicitly calls it one of OpenTable’s “**100 Most Romantic Restaurants in America**,” describes an Italian-villa-meets-Boston-mansion setting, and is set in historic North Square with skyline/cobblestone views. Google Maps calls it a “refined Italian menu … served in a romantic townhouse.” It also has an intimate two-seat **Piccolo** private dining room and says it can host intimate weddings—strong special-occasion evidence.
- **Italian / Boston seafood angle:** It is regional Italian using New England ingredients. The current sample menu includes **Duxbury baked oysters** and **Maine lobster agnolotti** ($48), alongside handmade pastas and classic Italian main courses.
- **Price level:** Google Maps reports **$50–100 per person**. The current menu lists antipasti at **$16–25**, pastas at **$39–48**, and mains at **$39–53**, before drinks/tax/tip.
- **OpenTable check:** I located the current OpenTable listing through search, but OpenTable itself blocked direct access in this browser. The listing result says Mamma Maria is **not available on OpenTable for booking**, so it does not expose real-time OpenTable inventory; the restaurant’s own site provides reservations/contact information.
- **Availability in the next two days:** **Not confirmed online / contact required.** The direct OpenTable booking path is unavailable and Mamma Maria’s on-site reservation control did not expose times here. Call **(617) 523-0077** to ask for September 30 or October 1, and mention the anniversary; the restaurant’s private-events material shows it regularly accommodates intimate celebrations.

In short: book **Ostra** for the polished business dinner and **Mamma Maria** for the romantic, Italian-and-Boston anniversary night. Both final official pages remain open, along with their Google Maps listings, so you can inspect photos, ambiance, and reservation links.

conversation.text: I’m in Boston for the next two days on a work trip with my wife, and I want to lock in two different dinners that feel right for each occasion. First, on the Michelin Guide site, please find me one Boston restaurant that’s Michelin-starred or clearly in that polished fine-dining tier for a business dinner, and keep it around a $500 per person ceiling so I know it’s appropriate without going overboard. Then switch to OpenTable and look for a separate restaurant in Boston that feels genuinely romantic for an anniversary dinner, ideally Italian seafood or something very Boston-specific, because I want the second night to feel more personal and celebratory. Once you have both, use Google to open the actual restaurant websites or current listing pages in separate tabs and verify that the business-dinner place really looks suitable for client-style dining and that the anniversary place clearly handles special occasions like anniversaries or romantic dinners; while you’re there, check whether each one appears to have availability sometime in the next two days. Please leave the final restaurant pages open so I can look at the photos, ambiance, and booking details myself, and give me a short summary of which place is for the business dinner and which is for the anniversary dinner, why each one fits, the expected price level, the special-occasion evidence you found, and the availability status for the next two days.
